name: Miramar
dining_districts: the commissary and food-production kitchens of the Miramar Park of Commerce
the Red Road corridor's Caribbean and Latin kitchens
intro: Miramar cooks for all of South Florida, not just itself. The Park of Commerce — one of the largest business parks in the region — is packed with commissaries, caterers, and food producers that need pallet-minded produce supply, while the Miramar Parkway and Red Road corridors serve one of the strongest Caribbean and Latin dining scenes in Broward: Jamaican, Cuban, Colombian, Peruvian kitchens with produce lists a generic supplier fumbles.

We stock for those lists — plantains, yuca, malanga, boniato, culantro, scotch bonnets alongside the standard restaurant staples — and we deliver them on the same 7-day refrigerated routes. Production kitchens get consistent case volume on schedule; restaurants get split cases and a midnight cutoff that respects how island kitchens actually order.
route_note: About 40 minutes southwest of our Pompano Beach warehouse — the far anchor of the south Broward loop, with commissary stops scheduled to production calendars.

faqs_unique.q: Do you carry Caribbean and Latin produce staples for Miramar kitchens?
faqs_unique.a: Yes. Plantains, yuca, malanga, boniato, culantro, hot peppers, and tropical fruit run on the same routes as standard restaurant staples — by the case or split case.

faqs_unique.q: Can you supply commissaries and food producers in the Park of Commerce?
faqs_unique.a: Yes. Production kitchens run consistent case-volume programs with scheduled delivery windows and volumes that track production calendars rather than dining covers.

cta_text: Tell us your commercial kitchen, commissary, restaurant, or group dining needs, and we will build a produce schedule around your Miramar receiving window and weekly throughput.
